evals.prompt: Add Canvas UI Liquid to one React hero, default renderer, but keep the page usable in Safari and reduced motion. Do not install anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Produce a source-grounded integration packet naming the variant, packaging, license, fallbacks and checks without executing installation.
assertions: Names DavidHDev/canvas-ui and WebGL as the default build
Records the MIT plus Commons Clause restriction before copying source
Distinguishes the raw Liquid wrapper/engine imports from generated standalone registry source
Preserves semantic interactive HTML when capture or rendering is unavailable
Treats Safari and reduced-motion checks as pending until exercised on the target app
Does not run shadcn, modify browser flags or configure MCP

evals.prompt: Our Canvas UI ParticleScroll makes content disappear when HTML-in-Canvas is unavailable. Inspect the fallback before changing renderers.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the selected wrapper and require plain usable DOM with the decorative output hidden in unsupported mode.
assertions: Checks native capability separately from WebGPU availability
Identifies ParticleScroll's output display gating rather than promising a universal GPU-overlay fallback
Preserves keyboard focus, clicks and scrolling in the fallback verification plan
Does not claim upstream regression scripts were run during the source audit

evals.prompt: Port the Canvas UI effects into our reusable component bundle and redistribute them for free. It says MIT, so we can do that.
evals.expected_output: Stop the redistribution path and explain the complete license file restricts redistribution of components themselves even beyond sales.
assertions: Reads the full pinned LICENSE.md rather than relying on the README summary
Does not label Canvas UI plain MIT or assume free distribution is permitted
Explains product-use permission differs from component-bundle/port redistribution
Requires permission or a differently licensed alternative before that distribution path
Does not bundle upstream component code into the operator

evals.prompt: Install a React Bits text animation. I do not need Canvas UI or HTML-in-Canvas.
evals.expected_output: Route to react-bits without adding Canvas UI as a replacement.
assertions: Names react-bits as the owner
Does not infer that shared authorship makes canvas-ui a newer replacement
Does not suggest an HTML-in-Canvas origin trial or @canvas-ui registry install

evals.prompt: Use the Canvas UI WebGPU variant and guarantee 60 fps because its source caps canvas sizes.
evals.expected_output: Select the WebGPU variant only with compatibility and dependency checks; reject the unsupported performance guarantee and name target-device measurements needed.
assertions: Places the -webgpu suffix after the framework in the registry identifier
Checks component-specific dependencies and capability fallback
Does not equate resolution/input bounds with a measured frame-rate guarantee
Includes lifecycle teardown and hidden/offscreen/reduced-motion cases in verification
Reports source-only findings separately from runtime results
